title: The earth swallowed him, and no one could help.
subtitle: What his wealth and servants could not do
then: After his pride and transgression against his people, {trap}Qarun and his dwelling were swallowed by the earth{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says his wealth, servants and retinue {trap}could not protect him{/trap}. He also cites hadith in Al-Bukhari and Ahmad about a man who walked in arrogance and was swallowed up.
now: You may have insurance, savings, connections. Good things. {idea}But the verse asks what any of it can do against Allah's decision.{/idea} Hold them lightly, and walk without arrogance.
old: With enough money and the right people, I am protected.
new: No wealth or group can protect anyone from Allah, so humility is my real safety.
try: Walk somewhere today slowly and humbly, making dhikr instead of checking your phone.

title: Yesterday they envied him. Today they were grateful.
subtitle: The crowd learns what wealth does not mean

row.title: His favor
sub: or we would be gone too

then: Those who had wished for his place {idea}began to say that Allah expands and restricts provision as He wills{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says wealth does not show Allah is pleased with its owner, citing Ibn Mas'ud: {reward}Allah gives wealth to those He loves and those He does not, but faith only to those He loves{/reward}.
now: You envied a classmate's life for years. Then you hear what was really going on behind the photos. {idea}Your heart turns to gratitude for what you were spared.{/idea} Faith, not money, is the sign of being loved.
old: Having more money means Allah loves someone more.
new: Allah gives wealth to many, but faith only to those He loves.
try: Thank Allah today for one thing you once wanted and did not get.

title: The final home is for those who seek no rank above others.
subtitle: Humility as the entry ticket
then: Ali said: {trap}if a man wants his sandal straps to be better than his companion's{/trap}, he is one of those meant here. Ibn Kathir explains that the problem is wanting to appear better than others. Simply liking to look good is fine: {reward}"Allah is beautiful and loves beauty."{/reward}
now: You pick the outfit for the wedding. Is it because you like it, or because you need to outshine your cousin? {idea}The verse is not against nice things. It is against wanting to be above people.{/idea}
old: Wanting to look good is the same as arrogance.
new: Liking beauty is fine; wanting to be above others is what closes the door.
try: Before you get dressed or post a photo today, ask: is this for me, or to be above someone?

title: Good returns better; evil returns only as much.
subtitle: Generosity for good, justice for evil
then: Ibn Kathir explains that {reward}Allah's reward is better than the servant's good deed{/reward}, since He multiplies it many times. Evil is repaid only by what was done. He calls this {idea}the position of generosity and justice{/idea}.
now: You helped your neighbour carry the shopping, five minutes of effort. Allah counts it as more than that. You snapped at your child; it is counted as exactly that, no more. {reward}The scale is tilted toward your good.{/reward}
old: My small good deeds hardly count against my mistakes.
new: Allah multiplies every good and counts every wrong only as itself, so good always gains.
try: Do three small good deeds today, each under five minutes.

title: The One who gave you the Quran will bring you back.
subtitle: A promise to the Prophet ﷺ while he faced opposition
then: Al-Bukhari recorded that Ibn Abbas said the "return" here means {reward}Makkah{/reward}: He will bring you back as He brought you out. Ibn Abbas also explained it as death, the Day of Resurrection, and Paradise. Ibn Kathir notes the Prophet ﷺ {idea}will be asked about the message entrusted to him{/idea}.
now: You had to leave: a home, a country, a job you loved. It feels like the door shut for good. {reward}The One who gave you your duties can bring you back{/reward}, to that place or to something better.
old: Once I have been pushed out of somewhere, it is over.
new: The One who entrusted me with my task can bring me back, in this life or the next.
try: Make dua today for one place or person you had to leave behind.

title: You never expected the Book. It came as mercy.
subtitle: An unexpected gift, and what follows from it

key.label: What a gift asks of you

row.title: loyalty
sub: do not help what opposes it

then: Ibn Kathir explains that before revelation came, the Prophet ﷺ {idea}did not expect it would be sent to him{/idea}. It was {reward}a mercy to him and to mankind because of him{/reward}. Having received such a blessing, he was told never to be a helper to those rejecting it.
now: You did not ask to be born into a home with the Quran on the shelf. You may have found it later, by surprise. {reward}It is a mercy you never earned.{/reward} The least you can do is not lend your effort to what pulls people away from it.
old: Having the Quran in my life is just how I grew up.
new: The Quran reaching me is an unexpected mercy, and I should not help anything that works against it.
try: Thank Allah today for the specific way the Quran first reached you.

title: Do not let opposition turn you away. Keep inviting.
subtitle: Staying steady when people push back

row.title: their opposition
sub: do not let it stop you

then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}do not let their opposition affect you{/idea} or put people off your way; do not worry about it. Allah will make the message prevail. So {idea}invite to your Lord{/idea}, to worship Him alone.
now: You started praying at work and someone made a joke. You shared a verse and got eye-rolls. {idea}Do not let that turn you away from what you know is true.{/idea} Keep going, gently.
old: If people push back, I should keep my faith to myself.
new: Opposition should not turn me from Allah's verses; I keep inviting, gently and steadily.
try: Share one beneficial verse or saying with someone today, kindly and without arguing.

title: Everything perishes except His Face.
subtitle: The last word of the surah
then: The surah that told of Fir'awn's tower and Qarun's treasure ends here. Ibn Kathir says Allah is {idea}Eternal, Ever Living{/idea}; while His creation dies, He never will. He cites the Prophet's ﷺ words that the truest line of a poet was {idea}"everything except Allah is false"{/idea}. To Him all return.
now: Your phone, your job title, the house, the body you look after. All of it is temporary, even the people you love. {idea}Only Allah remains.{/idea} Everything else is worth loving only as a way back to Him.
old: The things I build and own are what will last.
new: Everything perishes except Allah, so the only thing that lasts is what I do for Him.
try: Pick one thing you do every day and add a quiet intention for Allah to it.
